hints: Substitute $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$ to transform the equation into a quadratic in $\cos\theta$.
Factorise the quadratic and reject any root outside $[-1, 1]$.
Find the principal angle using $\cos^{-1}$ and the second angle using $360^\circ - \theta$.
walkthrough:
Use the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$ to write the equation in terms of $\cos\theta$ only:
$$3(1 - \cos^2\theta) = 4\cos\theta - 1 \implies 3 - 3\cos^2\theta = 4\cos\theta - 1$$

Rearrange into a standard quadratic equation and factorise:
$$3\cos^2\theta + 4\cos\theta - 4 = 0 \implies (3\cos\theta - 2)(\cos\theta + 2) = 0$$

Solve for $\cos\theta$, noting that $\cos\theta + 2 = 0$ yields no real solutions because $-1 \le \cos\theta \le 1$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{2}{3} \quad\text{or}\quad \cos\theta = -2 \text{ (no solution)}$$

Calculate the solutions for $\theta$ in the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 48.2^\circ$$
$$\theta = 360^\circ - 48.19^\circ \approx 311.8^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Equations: Applies $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$ to form quadratic $3\cos^2\theta + 4\cos\theta - 4 = 0$ (M1). Factorises and solves for $\cos\theta = \frac{2}{3}$ (A1). Obtains $\theta = 48.2^\circ$ (A1). Obtains second solution $\theta = 311.8^\circ$ (A1).
